new_task_1.title: Limit `Vary: Cookie` to responses that actually access the session
new_task_1.description: Flask 2.3.0 narrows when `SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session` adds the `Vary: Cookie` response header. The header is now only added when the session was actually accessed during request handling, instead of also being added whenever Flask refreshes, sets, or deletes the session cookie. This means responses that merely persist or clear session state without reading from the session become more cacheable and no longer vary on the `Cookie` request header by default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Flask only adds `Vary: Cookie` to a response when the request handler actually accessed the session data. Responses that merely cause the session cookie to be written, refreshed, or deleted without reading session contents should no longer automatically advertise variation on the `Cookie` request header.

expectation.grounded: In `SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session`, the `response.vary.add("Cookie")` call must be gated solely by `session.accessed`. The unconditional `Vary: Cookie` additions that previously occurred after deleting an empty modified session cookie and after writing a session cookie must be removed. The `session.accessed` check must occur after the empty-session early return path, so clearing an empty modified session no longer injects `Vary: Cookie` unless the session was otherwise accessed.
expectation.conceptual: A response should only declare that it varies by request cookies when application code actually depended on session contents. Merely updating session persistence state should not by itself mark the response as cookie-varying.

constraints.grounded: If a view reads from the session using operations such as item lookup, `get`, or `setdefault`, the response must still include `Vary: Cookie`. If the response already has a `Vary` header with other values, adding `Cookie` for an accessed session must preserve the existing entries. Session cookie writing and deletion behavior must remain unchanged; only the `Vary` header conditions change.
constraints.conceptual: The change must improve header accuracy without breaking session persistence itself. Cache variation should reflect actual session reads, not every response that happens to touch session storage mechanics.

behavior: Responses add `Vary: Cookie` when the session was accessed during request handling.
Responses no longer add `Vary: Cookie` solely because Flask writes or refreshes the session cookie.
Responses no longer add `Vary: Cookie` solely because an empty modified session causes the session cookie to be deleted.
Existing non-cookie `Vary` values remain present when `Cookie` is added for an accessed session.
Session cookie set/delete behavior is unchanged apart from the narrower `Vary` header emission.
acceptance_criteria: When a view reads from `flask.session` and returns a response, the response includes `Vary: Cookie`.
When a response already has `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language` and the session is accessed, the final header includes `Cookie` alongside the existing values.
When a request causes Flask to refresh a permanent session cookie without any session read in the view, the response does not include `Vary: Cookie`.
When a view clears an otherwise unread session and Flask deletes the session cookie, the response does not include `Vary: Cookie` unless the session was also accessed.
When a view does not touch the session at all, Flask does not add `Vary: Cookie`.
